title: Parameter-Efficient Periocular Fusion for Cross-Condition and Cross-Dataset Occlusion-Robust Face Verification
author: Pararajasingham Sangiya
target: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science
abstract: Masks and sunglasses remove different sources of facial identity information, making it unclear when a periocular representation should complement a whole-face model. We study this question using DINOv2, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), and five configurations ranging from a frozen encoder with a trained projection to dual-branch learned fusion. Fifteen models are trained for five complete epochs on CPU using three seeds and a 6,171-image ROF manifest that excludes known content conflicts. Periocular LoRA achieves the highest masked ROC-AUC (0.9221+/-0.0046), fixed fusion leads on sunglasses (0.8950+/-0.0021), and learned fusion leads on neutral faces (0.9458+/-0.0026). After excluding a known training-name overlap, learned fusion achieves 0.9548+/-0.0022 on 802 MFR2 pairs. Fixed fusion leads on 21,798 exact-conflict-excluded RMFRD pairs (0.7240+/-0.0099). Controls that retain the same trained branches show that image-dependent gate weights do not consistently improve on constant weights. Validation-calibrated thresholds also reveal false-accept shifts that retrospective ROC summaries conceal. A separate SFace diagnostic achieves higher AUC under different pretraining and alignment. The results support condition-dependent regional complementarity, while showing why neither the presence of a learned gate nor a high AUC alone establishes reliable verification under occlusion.
keywords: Face verification, occlusion robustness, masked-face verification, periocular representation, DINOv2, LoRA, learned fusion, cross-dataset evaluation.
